children: Shares of VA Tech Wabag Ltd. gained more than 1.5% on Monday, September 7, after the company said it has won a "medium" order from Reliance Industries Ltd (RIL) for an effluent treatment plant (ETP) in Jamnagar.
VA Tech Wabag classifies domestic orders within the ₹100 crore to ₹250 crore range as "medium".
It said the contract is for the design, engineering, manufacturing, supply, erection and commissioning of the ETP at the Dhirubhai Ambani Green Energy Giga Complex, Jamnagar.

The proposed ETP is scheduled to be completed in 13 months and will be designed comprising chemical and biological treatment using technologies and a sludge treatment incorporating low-temperature drying for efficient sludge management.

"This repeat order reinforces our long-standing relationship with RIL, a key customer, and reflects the continued trust and confidence RIL places in our capabilities," Sivakumar V, the company's senior general manager-sales and marketing, India cluster, said.
Last month, VA Tech Wabag said it signed a contract for the Doha SWRO desalination plant with recarbonation system - Stage II in Kuwait.

It said the order was awarded in June 2026 by Kuwait's ministry of electricity, water and renewable energy and the execution of the contract formally paved the way for the project to commence post the signing last month.
In July, the company informed the exchanges that it had bagged an order from the Bangalore Water Supply and Sewerage Board for two energy-efficient wastewater treatment facilities.
Shares of VA Tech Wabag gained over 1.8% in early trading on Monday at ₹2,040.9. The stock has now extended its year-to-date advance to 55%.

title: VA Tech Wabag shares gain after repeat order win from Reliance Industries for effluent treatment plant
